thread:
cheng: Heads-up, perf regression after the kernel-picker change landed on canary this morning. We're seeing more OOMs on 24GB workers and increased tail latency for long-context requests. flamegraph + allocation traces attached (short summary below). :eyes:

maria: ack, can you paste the top-line numbers?

cheng: median latency up ~6%, p99 up ~28% on long-ctx (>4k) traces. OOMs jumped from 0.02% -> 0.9% of requests on that fleet. GPU free memory variance widened (stddev free mem +45%).

alex: was the new kernel variant `opt_v2` selected for lots of layers? That one trades more workspace for fewer kernel launches, right?

cheng: exactly. kernel-picker started preferring `opt_v2` for attention when seq_len>1024 because of throughput win. But it allocs a contiguous workspace per request that ends up fragmenting the slab allocator under mixed-size KV cache footprints.

kyle: do we have a minimal repro? trace + small script to reproduce allocator fragmentation?

cheng: yes — reproducer attached in gist (link). Quick paste of the relevant log chunk:
```
[2026-03-17 09:14:22] kernel-picker: layer 7 -> opt_v2 (workspace=96MB)
[2026-03-17 09:14:22] allocator: slab 3 claim 110MB -> split into [64MB,46MB] (frag)
[2026-03-17 09:14:22] kv-cache: prefill + decode concurrent: 12 streams
[2026-03-17 09:14:22] OOM: failed to allocate 40MB transient workspace
```

maria: ugh. So concurrent prefill + decode is spiking transient peak and `opt_v2` increases transient envelope. We should consider per-request soft workspace caps and a fallback kernel with smaller working set.

alex: agreed. two immediate mitigations we can roll fast: 1) kernel-picker policy tweak: prefer `opt_v1` if predicted transient required > X MB; 2) introduce per-request soft cap that triggers queuing/delay for prefill or decode.

sabrina: propose a small config blob for canary. idea: prefer smaller-workspace kernel when predicted_work <-> kv_overlap_score > 0.5. config:
```
{
  "kernel_picker": {
    "workspace_threshold_mb": 48,
    "fallback_order": ["opt_v1","opt_v2"],
    "kv_overlap_bias": 1.2
  },
  "request_limits": {
    "soft_workspace_cap_mb": 128,
    "soft_action": "delay_prefill",
    "delay_ms": 20
  }
}
```

kyle: sounds reasonable. small delay_ms=20 should smooth spikes without hurting latency too much. Can we simulate restartless rollout in canary? ops-bot do we have a route to push as a runtime config only?

ops-bot: config flag pushed to canary ring: runtime-config/kernel-workspace-policy:v1 -> success on 8/8 nodes. No restart required.

maria: also want to try a different eviction heuristic: currently pure LRU across KV entries. With fragmentation we should prefer demoting large contiguous entries into a cold slab (coalesce) and prefer evicting small entries first to create large contiguous region for high-workspace kernels. Basically a fragmentation-aware eviction.

cheng: i sketched a heuristic: compute fragmentation_pressure = (largest_free_chunk_mb / total_free_mb). If pressure < 0.35, prefer demote_large_entries and schedule a background coalesce pass. Pseudocode:
```
if fragmentation_pressure < 0.35:
  eviction_order = sort_by(size, desc) // demote big entries first
else:
  eviction_order = LRU
```

alex: that makes sense. We should be careful about perf regressions for cold-start of demoted entries. Maybe keep a small hot-cache budget for recently-accessed demoted entries.

maria: timeline proposal: (1) push kernel-picker soft-threshold config to canary now (done), (2) enable soft_workspace_cap with delay_ms=15 on canary for 24h, (3) run synthetic mixed-load for 6h and collect OOMs/latency, (4) if green, roll to 30% traffic and enable fragmentation-aware eviction background pass.

cheng: metrics to watch: OOM rate, p50/p95/p99 latency for long-ctx, free_mem_stddev, avg fragmentation_pressure. Also track token throughput impact.

kyle: i can author a small perf-suite job that runs 10k mixed requests across seq lenses and records those metrics. putting it on my queue now.

sabrina: small note: model-serving infra should expose a callback to free ephemeral decode buffers earlier (we currently wait until request end). If kernel can be tweaked to yield earlier, could reclaim a chunk before prefill starts. I'll open a PR for callback hook.

ops-bot: perf-suite job queued: run-2241001234-frag-probe -> job id jf-7765. ETA 2h.

cheng: thanks. if perf-suite shows >5x reduction in OOMs with <2% throughput regression, i'm +1 to roll to 30%. otherwise we'll need to revert kernel-picker change.

alex: noted. i'll standby to revert kernel-picker patch if needed.

maria: great work triaging. keep notes in the incident doc under /incidents/frag-2241001234.md if we need postmortem.

cheng: will update after perf-suite finishes. :thumbsup:
